title: Heat engines & efficiency
examples: What is the maximum possible efficiency for any heat engine?
How does the temperature difference affect engine efficiency?
Can a refrigerator actually create energy?

explain.say: Today we explore how heat engines work and their efficiency limits. We will start with the concept of Carnot efficiency.

items: The Carnot cycle sets a maximum limit.

explain.say: The Carnot efficiency formula relates temperatures to efficiency. It uses the absolute temperatures of the hot and cold reservoirs.
A refrigerator moves heat from a cold space to a warmer area. This process requires external work input. This is different from an engine.
The efficiency of a refrigerator is related to the ratio of heat removed to work done. We call this the Coefficient of Performance.
For a refrigerator, the maximum performance is also set by temperature limits. It depends on the cold and hot temperatures.
In everyday life, think about keeping food cold in a fridge. The fridge moves heat from the inside to the room. It needs electricity to do this work.

faq.q: What is the difference between an engine and a refrigerator?
faq.a: An engine converts heat into useful work. A refrigerator uses work to move heat from one place to another.
asks: Does an engine make work from heat?

faq.q: Can I make an engine 100 percent efficient?
faq.a: No, according to the laws of thermodynamics, no heat engine can be 100 percent efficient. Some heat must always be rejected.

faq.q: Does the temperature difference matter for efficiency?
faq.a: Yes, the larger the temperature difference between the hot and cold sides, the higher the potential efficiency of the engine.
asks: Should I use hot or cold sources?

faq.q: What does 'absolute temperature' mean in the formulas?
faq.a: It means the temperature must be measured on a scale where absolute zero is zero. You must convert Celsius to Kelvin first.
asks: Do I use Celsius or Kelvin?
What scale for Th and Tc?

faq.q: Is the Carnot efficiency just a theoretical maximum?
faq.a: Yes, it represents the theoretical maximum efficiency. No real engine can reach this limit due to friction and other losses.
asks: What is the best real-world efficiency?

facts: Heat engines convert thermal energy into mechanical work.
Carnot efficiency sets the theoretical maximum efficiency for heat engines.
Refrigerators use work input to move heat from a cold space to a hot space.
Temperatures in thermodynamic calculations must be in Kelvin.

quiz.say: An engine operates between 300 Kelvin and 1000 Kelvin. What is its maximum efficiency?
quiz.why: The formula is 1 minus the cold temperature divided by the hot temperature, giving 0.7.

wrong.0: This incorrectly calculates the ratio of cold to hot temperatures.
wrong.1: This incorrectly subtracts the temperatures instead of taking the ratio.
wrong.2: This only calculates the ratio without subtracting it from one.

quiz.say: A refrigerator removes 500 Joules of heat and requires 100 Joules of work. What is its Coefficient of Performance?
quiz.why: The Coefficient of Performance is the heat removed divided by the work put in, which is 5.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the two energy values together.
wrong.2: This incorrectly subtracts the work from the heat removed.
wrong.3: This reverses the ratio, calculating work over heat removed.

quiz.say: If the cold reservoir is at 273 Kelvin and the hot reservoir is at 373 Kelvin, what is the maximum COP for the refrigerator?
quiz.why: The maximum COP uses the ratio of the cold temperature to the temperature difference, resulting in 2.73.

wrong.1: This incorrectly uses the hot temperature instead of the difference.
wrong.2: This calculates the temperature difference, not the COP ratio.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the temperatures in the denominator.
